name: framer-draggable-carousel

frames.best_why: A full portrait slide with both round arrows and the stretched active dot clearly visible.

tagline: Pull the photo sideways and it snaps to the next one.
summary: A full-width photo slider that moves when you grab and drag it, then springs onto the nearest image. Round arrows and a row of dots offer the same navigation without dragging.
appearance: One large photo at a time, about 400px tall, with softly rounded corners against a black page. A translucent white circle with a chevron floats at each side, and small white dots sit centred near the bottom, the current one stretched into a short bar.
behaviour: Dragging the photo back gives a little elastic resistance; on release the strip springs to the closest slide, or skips ahead when the flick is fast. Arrows and dots jump straight to a slide, and the arrow at either end fades to a disabled state.
demo_content: Twelve Unsplash photos: a bird over pale sky, cropped portraits of a woman, and blurred red-and-blue figures.
search_phrases: full width image slider with arrows
portfolio slideshow with round arrow buttons
one picture at a time banner slider
use_when: A wide image showcase should feel physical, with pulling as natural as clicking the arrows.
avoid_when: Slides are locked to 400px tall, and twelve image URLs sit hardcoded in the component file.
customise: Photos and titles are the items array in the file; spring stiffness, drag threshold and the 400px height need source edits.
weight_why: A strip of images moved by one transform, with a spring only after a drag.

a11y.note: Arrows and dots are real buttons but have no accessible names, and pictures are labelled with odd made-up titles.

issues: Dot buttons carry no label, so a screen reader cannot tell them apart.
Every slide is cropped to the same 400px height, cutting tall portraits.
polish_why: Crisp full-bleed photos and a convincing spring; unlabelled dots and odd titles hold it back.
title: Framer Draggable Carousel
